old_problem: The historical review correctly stopped an undefined security-policy write, but treated the standardized request fields as vendor-specific and therefore required an unavailable vendor schema. IPMI 2.0 defines the complete App 40h payload, volatile/non-volatile selectors, access/authentication/alerting flags, privilege values, readback and errors. The remaining channel, baseline, safe lower privilege and recovery path are Project execution parameters, not missing command semantics.
disposition_reason: Use the standard command through the in-band system interface so this unqualified identity remains distinct from row 1147's OOB variant. Target exactly one separately recoverable session-based management channel. Read both non-volatile and active baselines, then issue one volatile-only Set Channel Access that rewrites the active access/authentication/alert bits exactly unchanged while lowering only the channel privilege limit to an approved User or Operator value. Read back all fields, prove a least-privilege session still works, restore the exact active baseline and verify that non-volatile state, other channels, alerts and audit evidence never changed. No non-volatile selector, authentication weakening, mode toggle, privilege increase, retry, log clear or power/reset action is permitted.
decision_basis: Master XLSX rows 1020-1022 and 1024, exact same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT second review, tests_gpt_merged, selection manifest and historical V3.1 record were directly read. The exact code is unique. Row 1147 / Wistron-BMC-00437-V003 was directly read and preserves the separate Set Channel Access (OOB) identity. Formal queue sequence 61 was independently verified as row 1024 / variant f9d6813522808c27.

IPMI v2.0 section 22.22 defines App NetFn 06h command 40h. Request byte 1 is the actual channel number; byte 2 independently selects no change, non-volatile or volatile Channel Access; byte 3 independently selects no change, non-volatile or volatile Channel Privilege Level Limit.

Byte 2 bits 5:0 encode PEF alerting, per-message authentication, User-level authentication and access mode. Disabling either authentication option can permit unauthenticated traffic, so this case requires both to be enabled in the baseline and leaves every byte-2 low bit unchanged.

Byte 3 privilege values are Callback 1h, User 2h, Operator 3h, Administrator 4h and OEM 5h. This test only lowers the active limit to an approved 2h or 3h value that differs from baseline and never raises or writes a persistent limit.

Active settings are temporary and reload from non-volatile settings on reset or powered-off transition. That property bounds persistence but is not used as automated recovery: exact same-command restore and independent readback are mandatory, and this review performs no reset/power action.

Section 22.23 App 41h returns the selected non-volatile or present active access flags and privilege limit. It supplies a field-by-field pre/change/restore oracle; 82h means unsupported on the selected channel, 83h means access mode unsupported, and CCh can identify an unsupported optional field. None is PASS and no failure is retried.

The separate OOB source identity prevents crediting an OOB self-modification here. An in-band system-interface control path plus an independent observer ensures the command transport does not depend on the target channel and preserves distinct Coverage.

ED-02/ED-03/ED-13 support an exact standard BMC contract without OEM guesses; ED-15 governs authoritative unsupported N/A; ED-18/ED-30 require explicit security boundaries; ED-19 preserves evidence; ED-28 requires isolation/recovery; ED-33 through ED-38 govern package readiness, confirmation, cleanup, non-retry and engineer verdict separation.

test_case.test_name: IPMI Set Channel Access (App 06h/40h) in-band volatile privilege-limit change and exact restore
test_case.purpose: From an in-band system interface, validate standard Set Channel Access against one isolated session-based channel by preserving its access/authentication/alert bits, temporarily lowering only its active privilege ceiling, proving readback and least-privilege connectivity, and restoring the exact active baseline without changing persistent policy or the separate OOB variant's coverage.
required_package: Approved SUT/BMC/firmware, working local IPMI system interface and exact numeric target channel whose Get Channel Info proves it is session-based and is not the system-interface command channel or sole recovery path
Immutable App 41h baselines for target non-volatile selector 01b and active selector 10b, plus Get Channel Info, all-channel identity digest, active sessions, PEF/alert health and audit state

Project-approved safe lower active privilege 02h User or 03h Operator that differs from the current active baseline; current per-message and User-level authentication must both be enabled and access/PEF bits remain unchanged

Validated secret-safe IPMI raw runner/package implementing App 40h/41h bitfields, reserved-bit checks, explicit zero automatic retries, completion-code parsing, field comparator and finally-path restore; package version/hash
Dedicated probe identity at or below the temporary limit, independent OOB/physical recovery observer not using the target channel, exact baseline restore payload and security point confirmation
test_case.test_command: AUTHORIZED STATE-CHANGING PROCEDURE; DO NOT EXECUTE DURING REVIEW. Preserve audit/SEL and do not clear logs. Over the local system interface, prove target identity and obtain its actual numeric channel. Read App 41h twice: request [TARGET_CHANNEL,40h] for non-volatile and [TARGET_CHANNEL,80h] for active; decode response access byte and privilege byte, require authentication-enabled baseline and an owner-approved lower SAFE_PRIV in {02h,03h} different from active privilege. Display target, BASE_ACCESS_LOW6, BASE_ACTIVE_PRIV, SAFE_PRIV, exact payload and independent recovery, then obtain immediate approval. Send exactly once App 06h/40h request [TARGET_CHANNEL, 80h | BASE_ACCESS_LOW6, 80h | SAFE_PRIV]: both selectors are volatile, byte-2 access/auth/alert/mode bits are re-applied unchanged, and only privilege is lowered. Require completion 00h. Read active App 41h and require every access bit unchanged plus privilege SAFE_PRIV; re-read non-volatile and require byte-for-byte baseline. From the independent probe path, establish one dedicated session at or below SAFE_PRIV, issue read-only Get Device ID and close it. In a finally path, send exactly once [TARGET_CHANNEL, 80h | BASE_ACCESS_LOW6, 80h | BASE_ACTIVE_PRIV], require 00h, then read both active and non-volatile states and require exact original baselines. Verify other-channel digest, sessions, alert health and audit integrity. Never use selector 01b for a write, channel Eh as an inferred target, disabled/pre-boot/shared mode experiments, auth-disable bits, privilege increase, production credentials, OOB self-modification for this identity, reset/power actions, log clearing or automatic retry.
test_case.expected_result: The exact isolated session-based channel is selected. One volatile 40h write returns 00h; App 41h shows all six access/authentication/alert/mode bits unchanged and only the active privilege limit lowered to the approved User/Operator value. Non-volatile policy remains byte-for-byte unchanged. A dedicated session at or below the temporary limit completes a harmless Get Device ID and closes. The single restore returns 00h; active and non-volatile readbacks match their original baselines exactly, and other channels, sessions, PEF/alerting, management access and audit evidence are unchanged. 82h/83h/CCh, any generic error, timeout, unexpected bit, inability to probe/restore or collateral change is FAIL/NOT READY without retry; authoritative absence of a writable isolated session-based channel permits N/A.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires exact Source Key/variant, in-band transport distinct from the OOB variant, verified numeric target, immutable dual baseline, authentication-enabled access bits, one approved volatile-only payload, 00h completion, field-exact active readback with only the lower privilege delta, functional least-privilege probe, unchanged non-volatile/other-channel state, one exact restore and complete cleanup. A high-level `channel setaccess` user-policy command, non-volatile write, guessed bytes, selector/channel ambiguity, access/auth/alert/mode delta, privilege increase, only command success without App 41h proof, 82h/83h/CCh, hidden retry, target-channel-only recovery, reset/power recovery, persistent drift, lost alerts/access, log clearing or incomplete restoration cannot pass. Missing approved target/baseline/harness/recovery is NOT READY rather than Pending review.
safety_gate: The raw command must travel over the local system interface and target a different explicitly numbered session-based channel. The target may not be the only management/recovery channel; the independent observer must remain live throughout.
Write volatile selectors 10b only. Non-volatile selectors 01b, reserved 11b, broadcast/guessed channel values and bulk enumeration writes are prohibited.

Baseline must show per-message and User-level authentication enabled. Preserve PEF, authentication and access-mode bits exactly; only lower the active privilege ceiling to approved User/Operator and never use Administrator/OEM as the target delta.
Preserve logs and secrets. Confirm alerting and unrelated-channel digests before and after; do not clear SEL/dmesg/syslog or terminate unrelated sessions.
No automatic retry. A timeout is an ambiguous write: use independent App 41h readback to determine state, then perform only the owner-approved exact baseline restore once.

Stop on target mismatch, unsupported/invalid field, access or alert degradation, unexpected session effect, non-volatile change or uncertain restore. No host/BMC reset, power cycle or physical action is authorized by this review.
expected_evidence: Exact Source Key/variant; BMC/firmware/system-interface identity; target numeric channel and Get Channel Info session-support evidence; separate row-1147 OOB identity retained
Security approval, observer/recovery proof, runner version/hash, SAFE_PRIV rationale and redacted dedicated probe identity
Decoded immutable non-volatile and active App 41h baselines with raw-byte hashes, reserved-bit validation, auth/PEF/mode/privilege fields and all-channel/session/alert snapshots
Redacted single 40h volatile request, 00h response and active readback proving unchanged low-six access bits plus exact lowered privilege
Dedicated at-or-below-limit Get Device ID/close trace without unrelated operations
Single restore request/response, exact active/non-volatile baseline equality, unchanged other channels/sessions/alerts/audit/management health and engineer PASS/FAIL/NOT READY/N/A authority
test_case.recovery: Normal recovery is the precomputed volatile App 40h payload containing the exact captured BASE_ACCESS_LOW6 and BASE_ACTIVE_PRIV, sent once over the independent local system interface and verified by both active and non-volatile App 41h reads. On timeout, do not resend the change; first reconcile active state through the independent path, then execute only the approved restore if needed. If the system interface or target identity is uncertain, stop and have the BMC/security owner restore through the documented independent service path. Although IPMI reloads volatile settings from non-volatile state on reset/powered-off transition, this case must not trigger either action; any such recovery is separately authorized manual work. Preserve logs and verify access, alerts, sessions and all channel baselines before closure.

They may approve N/A only when authoritative platform evidence shows no suitable writable session-based channel. Approval cannot convert this row into the distinct OOB variant or permit non-volatile writes, authentication weakening, access-mode experiments, privilege increase, retries, log clearing, reset/power actions or incomplete restore.
